metadata.title: Arm Holdings beats Q1 estimates, but shares tumble

content.text:
Investing.com -- Arm Holdings reported first-quarter earnings per share of $0.45, surpassing analyst expectations of $0.37. The company posted revenue of $1.29 billion for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $1.27 billion.
Still, shares of ARM declined more than 6% in premarket trading on Thursday. The stock had already fallen 8.11% during the regular trading session.
For the second quarter of 2027, Arm Holdings projects earnings per share of $0.47, above the analyst consensus of $0.43. The company expects revenue of $1.38 billion for the period, compared to the consensus estimate of $1.34 billion.
The better quarterly results were driven by continued share and content gains in AI and data center chips, partly offset by near-term smartphone weakness.
Over the long term, Bank of America analysts believe Arm is well positioned to benefit from rising demand for agentic CPUs, across both its IP business — with key CSS products ramping in fiscal 2027-28 and increasing content per core over time — and its new AGI chiplet CPUs.
However, they warned that "investor expectations remain high" around both opportunities, and that "overall supply constraints cap any near-term upside."
BofA slashed its price target on the stock to $260 from $460 to reflect a "recent re-rating in peer multiple."
Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.
